drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted in animal milk; use caution in nursing mothers.
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 0.15mg/kg IV every 8 hours or 2mg-4mg PO TID in pediatric oncology.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: No dose adjustment required in renal impairment. In severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C), maximum daily dose is 8mg.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Safe when clinically needed; extensive human data indicates no increased risk of major malformations.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: 0.1mg/kg IV for post-operative nausea under pediatric anesthesia.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: No dose adjustment necessary; start at lower end of dosing range.
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: 0.15 mg/kg IV per dose in pediatric chemotherapy protocols.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), radiation-induced nausea (RINV), post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV).
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Acute gastroenteritis nausea in pediatric emergency settings, hyperemesis gravidarum.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Refractory pruritus associated with cholestasis, uremic pruritus.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Selective antagonist of 5-HT3 serotonin receptors located peripherally on vagal nerve terminals and centrally in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) of the area postrema.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapidly absorbed from GI tract; undergoes first-pass hepatic metabolism.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Oral Bioavailability: ~60%. Peak plasma level: 1.5 hours.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Extensively metabolized by hepatic CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2D6.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 3.5 - 5.5 hours (extended to 15-20 hours in severe hepatic impairment).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 30 minutes PO, 10 minutes IV. Peak: 1.5 hours PO. Duration: 8-12 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Hypersensitivity to ondansetron; concomitant use with apomorphine (profound hypotension and loss of consciousness).
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Congenital long QT syndrome, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, severe hepatic failure.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 QTc Prolongation Warning: Dose-dependent QTc interval prolongation. Avoid single IV doses > 16mg.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Serotonin Syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, or MAO inhibitors.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 May mask progressive ileus or gastric distension following abdominal surgery.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Monitor ECG in patients with electrolyte abnormalities or CHF.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Headache, constipation, fatigue, sensation of warmth or flushing, transient elevation of liver enzymes.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: QTc prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, severe bronchospasm, anaphylaxis.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Toxic epidermal necrolysis, oculogyric crisis, serotonin syndrome.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take with or without food. Food slightly increases oral absorption.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Severe hepatic impairment, cardiac arrhythmias, electrolyte disturbances.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Pediatric gastroenteritis, hepatic failure, cardiology patients with long QT.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: ECG (QTc interval), Serum Potassium, Serum Magnesium, LFTs in severe liver disease.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Take 30 minutes prior to chemotherapy or surgery. Dissolve orally disintegrating tablets on tongue.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take this medicine before meals or procedures to prevent nausea. Report any irregular heartbeat immediately.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Administer slow IV push over 2-5 minutes or IV infusion over 15 minutes. Check baseline QTc.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted in human milk; monitor infant for diarrhea, candidiasis, or sensitization.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 625mg PO q8h or 1000mg PO q12h; 1.2g IV q8h for severe infections.
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 30-45mg/kg/day in divided doses q12h (for 7:1 formulation) based on amoxicillin component.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: In CrCl 10-30 mL/min: max 625mg PO BID. In CrCl < 10 mL/min: max 625mg PO q24h. Contraindicated in history of amoxicillin/clavulanate-associated hepatic dysfunction.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Generally considered safe during pregnancy when clinically indicated.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Not recommended in neonates < 12 weeks with 1000mg or ES formulations.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Dose according to renal function; higher risk of GI upset.
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: Dosed strictly by mg/kg/day of Amoxicillin component.
drug_clinical_info.dialysis_considerations: Hemodialysis removes amoxicillin/clavulanate; administer supplemental dose post-dialysis.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Community-acquired pneumonia, acute bacterial sinusitis, otitis media, skin & soft tissue infections, UTI, bite wounds.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Exacerbation of COPD, dental infections, diabetic foot infections.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Surgical prophylaxis in pelvic or abdominal procedures.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis; Clavulanate irreversibly inactivates beta-lactamase enzymes produced by resistant bacteria.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Well absorbed after oral administration. Widely distributed into tissues and body fluids.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Oral Bioavailability: ~70%. Peak serum concentration in 1-2 hours.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: Amoxicillin 18%, Clavulanate 25%. Crosses placenta and breast milk.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Amoxicillin minimally metabolized; Clavulanate extensively metabolized in liver.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: ~1-1.3 hours. Excreted mainly by renal tubular secretion.
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: Rapid. Peak: 1-2 hours PO. Duration: 8-12 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to penicillins/cephalosporins; history of clavulanate-induced cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Mononucleosis (high incidence of erythematous skin rash); renal impairment.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Severe Anaphylaxis Warning: Cross-reactivity in patients with penicillin allergy.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Cholestatic jaundice and hepatitis may occur during or up to 6 weeks after therapy.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 High incidence of antibiotic-associated diarrhea and Clostridioides difficile colitis.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Monitor hepatic function, renal function, and hematopoietic status during prolonged therapy (> 14 days).
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, oral/vaginal candidiasis.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Cholestatic jaundice, hepatitis, erythema multiforme, urticaria.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, TEN, C. difficile-associated colitis, anaphylactic shock.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take at the start of a meal to enhance clavulanate absorption and minimize GI adverse effects.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Renal failure, infectious mononucleosis, hepatic dysfunction, gout (if taking allopurinol).
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Geriatric patients, patients with renal impairment, infants < 12 weeks.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: CBC with differential, LFTs (AST/ALT/Bilirubin), Renal function (BUN/Serum Creatinine).
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Swallow tablets whole at the start of a meal. Reconstituted oral suspension must be stored in a refrigerator (2-8°C) and discarded after 7-10 days.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store dry tablets below 25°C. Reconstituted liquid MUST be kept refrigerated and discarded after 7 days.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take this medicine with food or a snack. Finish the entire prescribed course even if you feel better.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Reconstitute powder with prescribed water volume. Shake well before each dose. Do not freeze.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted in human milk; decision should be made to discontinue nursing or drug.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 20mg-40mg PO once daily in the morning before breakfast for 4-8 weeks. (Zollinger-Ellison: up to 120mg TID).
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 10mg-20mg once daily for children > 1 year or > 10 kg.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: No dose adjustment needed in renal failure. In severe hepatic impairment, maximum daily dose is 20mg.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Animal studies show potential risk; use only if potential benefit outweighs risk.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Safety and efficacy not established in neonates.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: No initial dose adjustment necessary; higher risk of bone fractures with long-term use.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, H. pylori eradication (triple therapy), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: NSAID-induced ulcer prophylaxis, non-ulcer dyspepsia, stress ulcer prophylaxis in ICU.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Eosinophilic esophagitis, prevention of rebleeding from peptic ulcer.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme system (proton pump) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells, blocking the final step of gastric acid production.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Acid-labile; formulated as enteric-coated granules. Rapidly absorbed after passing stomach.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Bioavailability: 30-40% (increases to 60% with repeated doses). Peak plasma level: 0.5-3.5 hours.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: 95%. Distributed into liver, kidneys, and gastric mucosa.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Extensively metabolized by hepatic CYP2C19 (major) and CYP3A4 (minor).
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 0.5-1 hour (antisecretory effect lasts > 24-72 hours due to covalent binding).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 1 hour. Peak antisecretory effect: 2 hours. Duration: 24-72 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole or substituted benzimidazoles; concomitant use with rilpivirine.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Osteoporosis, hypomagnesemia, gastric malignancy (masking symptoms), Clostridioides difficile risk.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Long-Term Warning: Increased risk of bone fractures (hip, wrist, spine) with high-dose/long-term PPI therapy.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Severe hypomagnesemia reported in patients treated for > 1 year; B12 deficiency with long-term use.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 Interacts with clopidogrel (decreases active metabolite via CYP2C19 inhibition).
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Monitor serum magnesium prior to initiating PPI and periodically during prolonged treatment.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flatulence.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Hypomagnesemia, bone fracture, C. difficile diarrhea, acute interstitial nephritis.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reactions, subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take 30-60 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach with a glass of water.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Severe liver failure, osteoporosis/osteopenia, hypomagnesemia, active C. difficile infection.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Geriatric patients, chronic users (> 1 year), patients with hepatic impairment.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: Serum Magnesium, Vitamin B12 levels (long-term therapy), Bone Mineral Density (BMD) in high-risk patients.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Swallow capsules whole. Do not chew or crush enteric-coated granules.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture and excessive light.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take 30 minutes before your morning meal. Do not crush or chew the capsule.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers may experience 3-4 fold higher AUC. Consider pantoprazole if patient takes clopidogrel.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Present in human breast milk; monitor infant for hypotension or bradycardia.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 5mg-10mg PO once daily (Initial dose: 5mg once daily; max 10mg once daily).
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 2.5mg-5mg PO once daily in children 6-17 years.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: No dose adjustment necessary in renal impairment. Start at 2.5mg once daily in hepatic impairment.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Teratogenic in animal studies at high doses; use only if benefit outweighs fetal risk.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Safety not established in neonates and infants < 6 years.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Start at lower initial dose (2.5mg once daily) in frail elderly due to reduced clearance.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Essential hypertension, chronic stable angina, vasospastic angina (Prinzmetal angina), coronary artery disease.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Raynaud phenomenon, hypertensive urgency, diabetic nephropathy adjunct.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Inhibits influx of extracellular calcium ions across vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle membranes, relaxing coronary vascular smooth muscle and peripheral arterioles.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Slowly and almost completely absorbed from GI tract. Unaffected by food.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: 97.5%. Vd: ~21 L/kg. High tissue distribution.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Extensively metabolized by hepatic CYP3A4 to inactive metabolites.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 30-50 hours (extended in hepatic impairment and elderly).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: Gradual (6-12 hours). Peak: 6-12 hours. Duration: > 24 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Severe hypotension, cardiogenic shock, severe aortic stenosis, hypersensitivity to dihydropyridines.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Congestive heart failure (use with caution), hepatic impairment, elderly.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Severe Hypotension & Reflex Tachycardia Warning in patients with severe aortic stenosis.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Peripheral edema occurs in up to 10-15% of patients (dose-dependent).
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) increase amlodipine exposure.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Monitor Blood Pressure and Heart Rate before initiation and during titration.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Peripheral edema, flushing, dizziness, headache, fatigue, palpitations.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Severe hypotension, gingival hyperplasia, syncope, chest pain exacerbation upon initiation.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Anaphylaxis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, acute myocardial infarction (rare initial reflex).
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take with or without food. Avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice (may increase bioavailability).
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Severe aortic stenosis, severe hepatic impairment, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Geriatric patients, severe hepatic failure, pediatric hypertension.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, Liver Function Tests, Peripheral Edema assessment.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Take once daily at the same time each day with a glass of water.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture and direct light.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to prevent dizziness.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Long elimination half-life allows once-daily dosing. Max dose in hepatic impairment is 5mg daily.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted into human milk in low amounts; acceptable with infant monitoring.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 500mg-850mg PO BID/TID with meals; max 2550mg/day (IR) or 2000mg/day (XR).
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 500mg PO once or BID in children >= 10 years (max 2000mg/day).
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min. If eGFR 30-45 mL/min: max 1000mg/day. Withhold prior to iodinated contrast procedures in eGFR 30-60 mL/min.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: First-line oral agent in pregnant diabetic patients when insulin is not feasible.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Contraindicated in neonates and children < 10 years.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Lower dose recommendation; assess renal function prior to starting.
drug_clinical_info.dialysis_considerations: Hemodialysis clears metformin efficiently; do not use in end-stage renal disease unless on maintenance dialysis.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (first-line monotherapy or combination).
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), Gestational Diabetes, Prediabetes prevention.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), weight-gain prevention with antipsychotics.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Decreases hepatic glucose production (gluconeogenesis), decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake and utilization.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Slowly absorbed from small intestine. Unbound in plasma. Excreted unchanged in urine.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Bioavailability: 50-60%. Peak concentration: 2.5 hours (IR) or 7 hours (XR).
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: Negligible. Vd: 654 L. Accumulates in salivary glands, liver, and kidney.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Not metabolized by liver (excreted 100% unchanged by renal tubular secretion).
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 6.2 hours (plasma) / 17.6 hours (blood). Excreted in urine.
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 2-3 days for glycemic control. Peak: 2-4 weeks for full efficacy.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Severe renal dysfunction (eGFR < 30 mL/min), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (including diabetic ketoacidosis), severe dehydration, sepsis.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Renal impairment (eGFR 30-45 mL/min), hepatic impairment, chronic alcoholism, iodinated contrast imaging.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Boxed Warning: Lactic Acidosis — Rare but fatal accumulation in severe renal impairment, hypoxemia, or shock.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Withhold metformin at the time of or prior to iodinated contrast imaging procedures in patients with eGFR 30-60 mL/min.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 Long-term use associated with Vitamin B12 deficiency (monitor hematologic parameters).
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Monitor eGFR at least annually (q3-6 months in renal insufficiency) and serum Vitamin B12 every 2-3 years.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, metallic taste, anorexia.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Lactic acidosis, severe Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia, hypoglycemia (when combined with insulin/sulfonylurea).
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Lactic acidosis with severe cardiovascular collapse.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take with or immediately after meals to minimize gastrointestinal upset.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Renal failure (eGFR < 30), severe liver failure, heart failure requiring pharmacologic intervention, acute alcoholism.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Renal impairment, elderly patients, patients undergoing radiology with contrast.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: eGFR / Serum Creatinine, HbA1c, Fasting Blood Glucose, Vitamin B12 level, Complete Blood Count.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Take with meals. Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or break.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store below 25°C in a tight container.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take this medicine with food to avoid stomach upset. Limit alcohol consumption.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Renal tubular secretion substrate (OCT2). Co-administration with dolutegravir increases metformin levels.

drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 12 mg/kg/day IV for 4 consecutive days (Max: 800 mg/day).
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: Pediatric dosing strictly protocol-dependent under oncology supervision.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Use with caution in renal or hepatic impairment; monitor DPD enzyme activity.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Teratogenic and embryotoxic. Absolute contraindication in pregnancy.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Dose reduction required in frail elderly patients with cardiac insufficiency.
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: Calculated based on Body Surface Area (mg/m²).
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Colorectal carcinoma, breast carcinoma, gastric and pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Topical treatment of actinic keratosis and superficial basal cell carcinoma.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Irreversibly inhibits thymidylate synthase, blocking DNA synthesis.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapid IV clearance; metabolized hepatically by dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD).
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: IV Bioavailability: 100%. Oral absorption is erratic.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Hepatic degradation via DPD enzyme pathway.
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Peak plasma concentrations immediately after IV bolus.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Severe DPD enzyme deficiency, bone marrow suppression, severe infection.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Cardiac disease, history of myocardial ischemia.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Boxed Warning: Severe toxicity and fatalities in patients with dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Stomatitis, severe diarrhea, neutropenia, and hand-foot syndrome.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 Monitor CBC with differential daily during induction.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Weekly CBC, LFTs, and renal function.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Myelosuppression, cardiotoxicity, severe enteritis, hand-foot syndrome.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Avoid alcohol and concurrent warfarin (increases INR).
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Geriatric patients and patients with dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase gene variants.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: CBC, Platelets, LFTs, Bilirubin, Cardiac telemetry if symptomatic.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Administer via central or peripheral IV infusion per oncology protocol.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Report signs of fever, severe diarrhea, or chest pain immediately.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Pharmacist double-check required for all chemotherapy dosing and calculations.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted in human milk; avoid during breastfeeding.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 2mg-10mg PO 2 to 4 times daily, or 10mg IV/IM for status epilepticus.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Avoid in severe hepatic impairment; dose reduction required in renal impairment.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Risk of congenital malformations in 1st trimester. Neonatal withdrawal.
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Not recommended in neonates due to benzyl alcohol preservative risks.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Start at 2mg PO once or twice daily (risk of ataxia and confusion).
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: Dosed by weight in pediatric status epilepticus.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Anxiety disorders, acute alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasm, status epilepticus.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Akathisia, night terrors, severe refractory insomnia.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Binds to stereospecific benzodiazepine receptors on postsynaptic GABA-A neuron site, enhancing GABA inhibitory effects.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapid oral absorption; extensively metabolized by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 to active metabolites (desmethyldiazepam).
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Hepatic via CYP2C19 & CYP3A4 to active metabolite desmethyldiazepam.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination half-life: 20-50 hours (active metabolite up to 100 hours).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: IV onset: 1-5 min; Oral onset: 15-30 min.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Myasthenia gravis, severe respiratory insufficiency, severe hepatic failure, sleep apnea.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: 🔴 Boxed Warning: Concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: 🟠 Abuse, misuse, addiction, physical dependence, and severe withdrawal reactions.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: 🟡 Elderly patients have increased risk of fall and cognitive impairment.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: 🔵 Respiratory rate, blood pressure, sedation score, hepatic function.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Respiratory depression, hypotension, dependence, paradoxical excitation.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Laryngospasm, coma, fatal overdose with CNS depressants.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Respiratory disease, hepatic impairment, substance use disorder.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: Respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, sedation depth.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Administer IV slowly (5mg/min). Avoid rapid bolus to prevent apnea.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Do not drive or operate machinery while taking this medicine. Avoid alcohol.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Controlled Schedule IV drug. Verify security storage and logbook entry.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Excreted in small amounts in breast milk; compatible with breastfeeding.
drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 275mg to 550mg PO every 12 hours as needed (or 550mg initially followed by 275mg every 6-8 hours; Max: 1375mg/day).
drug_clinical_info.pediatric_dosage: 10mg/kg/day PO divided into 2 doses for juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children >= 2 years.
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Avoid in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min). Monitor renal and hepatic parameters during prolonged therapy.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Category C prior to 20 weeks; Category D starting at 20 weeks gestational age (oligohydramnios and premature ductus arteriosus closure).
drug_clinical_info.neonatal_dosage: Safety and efficacy not established in neonates.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Initiate with lowest effective dose (275mg BID); increased risk of GI hemorrhage and renal impairment.
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: 10mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses for pediatric arthritis.
drug_clinical_info.dialysis_considerations: Not dialyzable due to high protein binding (> 99%).
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Acute musculoskeletal pain, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, tendonitis, bursitis, acute gout, primary dysmenorrhea.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Migraine headache treatment and prophylaxis, fever, post-operative dental pain.
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Paget disease of bone, heterotopic ossification prophylaxis.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and 2 (COX-1 and COX-2) enzymes, blocking conversion of arachidonic acid to inflammatory prostaglandins.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapid and completely absorbed from GI tract; extensive hepatic metabolism via CYP2C9 and CYP1A2.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Oral Bioavailability: 95%. Peak plasma concentration: 1-2 hours.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: > 99%. Volume of distribution: 0.16 L/kg.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Extensively metabolized in liver by CYP2C9 and CYP1A2 to 6-O-desmethylnaproxen.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 12-17 hours (permits twice-daily dosing). Renal excretion: 95%.
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 30-60 minutes for analgesia. Peak: 1-2 hours. Duration: 12 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Hypersensitivity to naproxen, aspirin, or other NSAIDs; CABG surgery setting; active gastrointestinal bleeding or peptic ulcer disease.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Hypertension, congestive heart failure, chronic kidney disease, cirrhosis, history of GI bleed.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: Boxed Warning: Cardiovascular Risk (MI, Stroke) and Gastrointestinal Risk (Bleeding, Ulceration, Perforation). Naproxen has lowest cardiovascular risk among non-selective NSAIDs.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: Renal toxicity including papillary necrosis and acute interstitial nephritis with long-term use.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: Fluid retention and edema; can worsen pre-existing heart failure.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: Baseline and periodic CBC, renal function (BUN/Creatinine), blood pressure, and occult fecal blood.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Dyspepsia, heartburn, nausea, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, edema.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: GI bleeding, peptic ulcer, acute renal failure, severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS/TEN).
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_rare_life_threatening: Anaphylaxis, fatal GI perforation, Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take with food or milk to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort. Avoid concurrent alcohol.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Peptic ulcer disease, hypertension, heart failure, renal insufficiency, aspirin-sensitive asthma.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Elderly, patients with cardiovascular risk factors, third trimester of pregnancy.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: Blood pressure, Serum Creatinine, BUN, Complete Blood Count, LFTs.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Take with a full glass of water, with or after food. Do not lie down for 15 minutes after taking.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store at 20-25°C. Protect from light and excessive moisture.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take with food or milk to avoid upset stomach. Stop taking and call your doctor immediately if you experience dark/black stools, persistent stomach pain, or chest pain.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Lowest CV risk profile among traditional NSAIDs (ADAPT trial). Take low-dose cardioprotective aspirin 30-60 minutes prior to naproxen.

drug_clinical_info.adult_dosage: 100mg PO every 12 hours (morning and evening with food; Max: 200mg/day).
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Start at 100mg once daily in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment. Avoid in severe renal or hepatic failure.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Avoid in pregnancy, particularly in third trimester (risk of premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus).
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: No initial dose adjustment; start with lowest effective dose.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute lumbago, dental pain, post-traumatic pain.
drug_clinical_info.indications_common: Dysmenorrhea, acute musculoskeletal sprain and strain.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Potently inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme with preferential selectivity for COX-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis while demonstrating superior gastric tolerability compared to conventional diclofenac.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapidly and completely absorbed from gastrointestinal tract; metabolized in liver.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Oral Bioavailability: Close to 100%. Peak plasma level: 1.5 - 3 hours.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Protein Binding: > 99%. Volume of distribution: ~25 L.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Metabolized in liver via CYP2C9 to 4-hydroxyaceclofenac.
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 4-4.5 hours. Excreted mainly through kidneys (70-80%).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 30 minutes. Peak: 1.5-3 hours. Duration: 12 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding; hypersensitivity to aceclofenac, diclofenac, or aspirin; severe heart failure; severe renal/hepatic impairment.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Hypertension, mild-to-moderate heart failure, ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease.
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: Cardiovascular & GI Risk Warning: Potential for increased thrombotic events and gastrointestinal ulceration.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: Hepatic transaminase elevation reported in rare cases; monitor LFTs in prolonged treatment.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: May trigger bronchospasm in patients with bronchial asthma or allergic disease.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: LFTs (AST/ALT), renal function, CBC with differential.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Dyspepsia, abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, pruritus.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: GI hemorrhage, peptic ulcer, severe nephrotoxicity, hepatic necrosis.
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Take preferably with or after food to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Peptic ulcer disease, ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Elderly patients, patients with cardiovascular risk factors.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: Blood pressure, Serum Creatinine, Liver Function Tests.
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Swallow tablets whole with water. Do not crush or chew. Take with or after meals.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store below 30°C in a dry place.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Take this medicine after meals. Report any stomach pain, nausea, or dark-colored stools to your pharmacist.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Superior gastrointestinal safety profile compared to diclofenac due to preferential COX-2 inhibition and minimal suppression of gastric mucosal PGE2.

drug_clinical_info.lactation_safety: Compatible with breastfeeding (small amounts in milk).
drug_clinical_info.hepatic_renal_precautions: Contraindicated in severe active liver failure. Reduce max dose to 2000mg/day in chronic alcohol abuse or hepatic insufficiency. In CrCl < 10 mL/min, extend interval to q8h.
drug_clinical_info.trimester_considerations: Safe across all trimesters at recommended doses; avoid excessive duration.
drug_clinical_info.geriatric_dosage: Use lowest effective dose; start with 500mg in frail elderly.
drug_clinical_info.weight_bsa_dosing: Dosed strictly by mg/kg in children.
drug_clinical_info.dialysis_considerations: Slightly dialyzable (HD/PD); no supplemental post-dialysis dose required unless prolonged.
drug_clinical_info.indications_approved: Fever reduction, mild-to-moderate pain (headache, toothache, dysmenorrhea, musculoskeletal pain).
drug_clinical_info.indications_offlabel: Patent ductus arteriosus closure in preterm infants (IV formulation off-label).
drug_clinical_info.pharmacology_moa: Reversibly inhibits central cyclooxygenase (COX-1 & COX-2) pathways in CNS, inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis and elevating pain threshold.
drug_clinical_info.pharmacokinetics_summary: Rapid oral absorption; hepatic glucuronidation and sulfation; minor NAPQI toxic metabolite pathway via CYP2E1 detoxified by glutathione.
drug_clinical_info.absorption_bioavailability: Oral Bioavailability: 88-90%. Peak plasma concentration reached in 30-60 minutes.
drug_clinical_info.distribution_protein_binding: Vd: ~1 L/kg. Low protein binding (10-25%). Crosses placenta and blood-brain barrier.
drug_clinical_info.metabolism_cyp: Metabolized in liver via glucuronidation (55%), sulfation (30%), and CYP2E1 (5-10% NAPQI).
drug_clinical_info.half_life_elimination: Elimination Half-life: 2-3 hours. Renal excretion of metabolites (90% in 24h).
drug_clinical_info.onset_peak_duration: Onset: 15-30 min PO, 5-10 min IV. Peak: 1 hour PO. Duration: 4-6 hours.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_absolute: Hypersensitivity to paracetamol; severe acute liver disease or active hepatic failure.
drug_clinical_info.contraindications_relative: Chronic alcohol abuse, malnourishment, severe renal impairment (eGFR < 15 mL/min).
drug_clinical_info.boxed_warnings: Overdose Warning: Doses > 4g/day cause fatal acute liver necrosis. N-acetylcysteine antidote required within 8 hours.
drug_clinical_info.serious_warnings: Hepatotoxicity risk in malnourished or chronic alcoholic patients.
drug_clinical_info.cautions: Avoid concurrent paracetamol-containing combination products to prevent accidental overdose.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_required: Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) if therapy exceeds 10 consecutive days.
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_common: Nausea, rash, headache, constipation (with IV route).
drug_clinical_info.side_effects_serious: Hepatotoxicity, severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, TEN).
drug_clinical_info.food_interactions: Food slightly delays peak absorption rate but does not reduce overall bioavailability. Avoid heavy alcohol consumption.
drug_clinical_info.disease_interactions: Severe hepatic dysfunction, chronic hepatitis, alcohol dependency, G6PD deficiency.
drug_clinical_info.special_populations: Hepatic insufficiency, chronic alcohol use, pediatric weight-based dosing.
drug_clinical_info.monitoring_parameters: LFTs (AST/ALT, Bilirubin) in prolonged use or overdose, Serum Paracetamol level (Rumack-Matthew nomogram).
drug_clinical_info.administration_instructions: Take with a full glass of water. Can be taken with or without food. Do not crush sustained-release tablets.
drug_clinical_info.storage_stability: Store below 30°C in a cool, dry place. Protect from excessive light and humidity.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_en: Do not take more than 8 tablets (500mg each) in 24 hours. Check labels of cold/flu products so you do not double dose.
drug_clinical_info.patient_counseling_professional: Verify patient total daily dose from all combined OTC and Rx products. Administer IV infusion over 15 minutes.
